prompt: In a random sample of $400$ commuters, $160$ say they bike to work at least once a week. For a $95\%$ confidence interval for the true proportion, using $z^* = 1.96$, what is the margin of error? Round to three decimal places.
hint: Margin of error $= z^* \times SE$, where $SE = \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}$.

hints.text: Margin of error $= z^* \times SE$, where $SE = \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}$.

explanation: Margin of error: $1.96 \times 0.0245 \approx 0.048$. The interval is about $0.40 \pm 0.048$, or $(0.352, 0.448)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the conditions first
steps: Random sample ✓. Successes $160 \ge 10$ and failures $240 \ge 10$ ✓. 400 is surely less than $10\%$ of all commuters ✓.
With conditions met, the one-proportion $z$-interval applies: $\hat{p} \pm z^* \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}$.
